units.function: HTTP route regression suite serving plain-text Paperclip Agent configuration and static Hermes Gateway setup documentation.
units.dependencyDirection: The route reads built-in/static documentation plus server adapter descriptors; it does not call an LLM, provider SDK, secret store or tenant data service.
units.keyDataModels: Board actor, adapter type and agentConfigurationDoc; plain-text hiring/heartbeat instructions; Hermes adapter, environment-variable and network endpoint examples.
units.lifecycle: Request documentation index or named Hermes configuration text and assert literal installation/configuration guidance is present.
units.testAssessment: Two HTTP cases pass outside the sandbox and protect availability of Paperclip/Hermes setup prose. They do not assert authorization, content type/cache/version, redaction or any model-provider behavior. Heavy literal-English assertions make tests sensitive to documentation wording rather than stable capability contracts.
units.designRationale: Make adapter onboarding instructions discoverable through the running server, including before an optional plugin is installed.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral model and Agent capability management, tenant-owned credential references, data-use policy, cost/rate controls and clear onboarding documentation without coupling product behavior to a vendor's prose.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT direct reuse. Define ModelProviderPort with stable provider/model IDs, declared modalities/context/tool/region capabilities, health, pricing snapshot, data-retention/training policy, credentialRef, tenant scope and structured failure codes. Keep Connector onboarding docs as versioned documentation generated from capability manifests, not an /llms route whose tests depend on English text. Adapter-specific Hermes guidance, if ever needed, belongs solely in a Hermes connector package and must not become the canonical model abstraction.
units.responsibilityConflict: The documentation endpoint gives operational setup instructions but carries no accountable human, approved credential/data scope or policy receipt. Treating it as a model-management surface would let configuration prose substitute for enforceable governance.

2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 2/2 failed on TCP EPERM only
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL capability-evidence gap: no credential isolation, provider tenancy, data-governance, cost, rate, inference or failover behavior is present despite the llms route name. HIGH authorization gap: an admin-like actor is supplied but no denial/role test proves the docs are access controlled. MEDIUM operational-disclosure risk: internal/LAN/tailnet/Docker endpoint patterns and key variable names are published, though no actual secret value appears in the fixture. MEDIUM contract risk: exact English documentation strings are treated as API behavior.
